results.question: what does 'up to 50 days interest free' actually mean? do I get 50 days on everything I buy with the credit card?
results.answer:

A purchase made on the first day of a statement period waits the longest before it is due, so it gets the full 50 days. A purchase made on the last day of a statement period gets the fewest days.

For example, with a statement period from 1 May to 31 May and a due date of 20 June:
- Buying on 1 May gives 50 days.
- Buying on 15 May gives 36 days.
- Buying on 31 May gives 20 days.

The interest-free period applies only when you pay your full statement balance by the payment due date. It also does not apply to cash advances. Our app shows your statement date and your next payment due date, so you can see your own dates.

results.question: how is the personal loan interest worked out, is it linked to the base rate?

We write to you in the app before the change takes effect, telling you the new rate, your new instalment and the date it starts.

Interest is worked out monthly on what you still owe. Each month, interest is the monthly rate (15.5% divided by 12) applied to the balance you owe at the start of that month. Your instalment pays that month's interest first, and the rest reduces the balance. So the interest part shrinks over time as you repay.
